mainTopic: Who is obligated in the מצוה of ראייה (appearing in the בית המקדש on the רגלים), and what the word הכל in the משנה comes to include
overview: The משנה opens מסכת חגיגה by saying everyone must come to the בית המקדש on the three רגלים, except for a list of people who are exempt. It then records two disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל: how small a child must be to count as a קטן for this מצוה, and the minimum value of the עולת ראייה and the שלמי חגיגה. The גמרא asks what extra case the word הכל ("all") comes to include, and first answers: a person who is half slave and half free. Since רבינא exempts that person, the גמרא offers another case: someone lame on the first day of the רגל who healed on the second day. That case only works if every day of the רגל counts on its own, so for the other view the גמרא suggests someone blind in one eye. It notes that this goes against a ברייתא of יוחנן בן דהבאי in the name of רבי יהודה, who exempts such a person. Finally, the גמרא returns to the half-slave answer and explains that it and רבינא follow an earlier and a later version of a משנה. It begins quoting that משנה, and בית שמאי's reply continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Everyone must appear on the Festivals, except a list of exempt people
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says all are obligated in ראייה, and lists who is exempt: חרש, שוטה, קטן, טומטום, אנדרוגינוס, women, unfreed slaves, the lame, the blind, the sick, the old, and anyone who cannot walk up on his own legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone has to go up and appear at the בית המקדש on the רגלים, except a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, a minor, a טומטום, an אנדרוגינוס, women, slaves who were not freed, the lame, the blind, the sick, the old, and anyone who cannot go up on foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states the basic rule: everyone must appear in the בית המקדש on the רגלים. Then it lists the people who are exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule starts very wide with הכל ("all") and then narrows it with a list of exceptions. The last group, the lame, blind, sick, old and anyone who cannot walk up, are people who cannot fully go up and appear. The גמרא learns each of these exemptions from פסוקים (for example, the blind from the reading יִרְאֶה / יֵרָאֶה). The גמרא will soon ask what the wide word הכל adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Appearing in the בית המקדש on the רגלים and bringing an עולה offering
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor, the classic group with limited legal responsibility
A person whose gender cannot be determined
A person with both male and female features
A lame person

steps.whyThisMatters: This list sets the boundaries of the מצוה. The rest of the סוגיא will study it closely.

phrases.english: All are obligated in appearance,
phrases.notes: "Appearance" means coming to be seen at the בית המקדש on the three Festivals.

phrases.english: except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
and a tumtum and a hermaphrodite,
and women, and slaves who are not freed,
the lame and the blind,
and the sick and the old,
and one who is unable to go up on his own legs.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone is obligated in ראייה except the listed categories.

steps.title: How small a child counts as a minor for this מצוה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say a קטן is any child who cannot ride on his father's shoulders from ירושלים up to הר הבית. בית הלל say it is any child who cannot hold his father's hand and walk up, based on the פסוק "שלש רגלים".
steps.simpleTranslation: Who counts as a קטן here? According to בית שמאי, a child too young to ride up on his father's shoulders from ירושלים to הר הבית. According to בית הלל, a child too young to hold his father's hand and walk up, since the פסוק says "שלש רגלים" (which hints at feet).
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains which "minor" it meant in the list of exemptions. בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not about the usual age of a קטן (בר מצוה). It is about which young children the father must bring along. For בית שמאי, even a child who must be carried is included. For בית הלל, only a child who can walk is included, because the word רגלים points to going up on one's own feet. So בית הלל exempt more children than בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: The students of שמאי
The students of הלל
The Temple Mount
"Three times" (literally "three feet"), the פסוק about going up three times a year

steps.confusionAlert: This קטן is not the regular under-בר-מצוה definition. The question here is which young children the father must bring to the בית המקדש, which is a rabbinic level of obligation for training.

phrases.english: Who is a minor?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִרְכּוֹב עַל כְּתֵפָיו שֶׁל אָבִיו
phrases.english: Any child who is unable to ride on his father's shoulders
and go up from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount,
these are the words of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לֶאֱחוֹז בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו
phrases.english: Any child who is unable to hold his father's hand
and go up from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount,
as it is said: "Three times [regalim]."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:14. The word רגלים sounds like רגליים, "feet," so בית הלל learn that this is about walking up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term קטן from the list of exemptions in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: a child who cannot be carried on his father's shoulders is exempt. בית הלל: a child who cannot walk holding his father's hand is exempt.

steps.title: Minimum value of the appearance offering and the Festival offering
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say the עולת ראייה must be worth at least two silver coins and the שלמי חגיגה at least one מעה. בית הלל reverse it: the ראייה is one מעה and the חגיגה is two silver coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי: the appearance offering costs at least two silver coins, and the Festival offering at least one silver מעה. בית הלל: the appearance offering is at least one silver מעה, and the Festival offering at least two silver coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל, this time about the smallest amount a person may spend on each of the two Festival offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate קרבנות here: the ראייה, which is an עולה burned completely, and the חגיגה, which is a שלמים that is eaten. The two schools use the same two amounts but switch which offering gets the larger one.

keyTerms.meaning: The Festival peace-offering (שלמים) brought on the רגל
A small silver coin
Two silver coins

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts: who is obligated, who counts as a קטן, and the minimum value of the ראייה and חגיגה offerings.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
The appearance offering, two silver coins,
and the Festival offering, one silver ma'a.
And Beit Hillel say:
The appearance offering, one silver ma'a,
and the Festival offering, two silver coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: הָרְאִיָּיה שְׁתֵּי כֶסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new dispute in the same משנה, about the value of the offerings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: ראייה 2 silver, חגיגה 1 מעה. בית הלל: ראייה 1 מעה, חגיגה 2 silver.

steps.title: What does the word "all" come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the word הכל in the משנה adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said "All are obligated." What is the word "all" adding?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about the first word of the משנה. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have just listed who is exempt. The extra word הכל suggests that some case which might have seemed exempt is in fact obligated. The גמרא wants to know which case that is.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
"To include what?", asking what an extra word adds

phrases.english: Gemara
"All" comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by asking about the first word of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is added by the word הכל?

steps.title: "All" includes a half-slave, half-free person
steps.stepSummary: The word הכל includes someone who is חציו עבד וחציו בן חורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a person who is half slave and half free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that הכל teaches that a half-slave, half-free person is obligated in ראייה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempted slaves who are not freed. Someone who is only half freed might seem to fall under that exemption. The word הכל tells us he is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is half slave and half free, for example one owned by two partners where only one partner freed him

phrases.english: To include one who is half slave
and half free.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל includes a person who is half slave, half free.

steps.title: According to רבינא, what does "all" include?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא holds that a half-slave, half-free person is exempt. So according to him, what does הכל include?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבינא said that someone who is half slave and half free is exempt from ראייה. According to him, what does "all" include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the first answer does not work for רבינא, so it asks the question again according to his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבינא exempts the half-slave, the answer of step 5 cannot be his explanation of הכל. This does not reject the first answer. It only means רבינא needs a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt

phrases.english: And according to Ravina, who said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
phrases.english: one who is half slave and half free
is exempt from the appearance,
"All" comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of step 5 does not fit רבינא and asks the question again
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבינא, which case does הכל include?

steps.title: "All" includes one who was lame on the first day and healed on the second
steps.stepSummary: According to רבינא, הכל includes someone who was lame on the first day of the רגל and healed on the second day. He is obligated to appear.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include someone who was lame on the first day of the Festival and got better on the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבינא's answer: הכל teaches that a person who was lame on day one but healed on day two still has to appear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lame person is exempt. We might think that being exempt on the first day exempts him for the whole Festival. הכל teaches that once he heals while the Festival is still going on, he becomes obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally "straightened out," meaning his leg healed
The first day of the Festival

phrases.english: To include one who was lame on the first day
and was healed on the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 according to רבינא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל includes one who was lame on the first day and healed on the second day.

steps.title: The lame-person answer only works for one view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבינא's case of someone lame on the first day only works for the view that every day of the רגל can make up for every other day. For the view that the later days only make up for the first day, הכל still needs a new case.
steps.simpleTranslation: That answer works for the one who says all the days make up for one another. But for the one who says all the days only make up for the first day, what does the word 'all' add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 7. It shows that the answer depends on one specific view about the days of the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every day of the רגל is a full day of obligation, a person who heals on the second day becomes obligated then. But if the later days are only make-up days for the first day, then someone who was exempt on the first day stays exempt the whole רגל. So for that view, the lame person is not included, and הכל needs a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view, but not for another)
Make-up days for a מצוה that was missed
All the days make up for one another, so each day is a full day of obligation
All the days only make up for the first day, which is the main day

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question against the half-slave answer. It is a question on רבינא's own answer, the lame person who healed.

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who said
all of them are make-up days for one another.
phrases.notes: He means all seven days of the רגל. Any day can count for the מצוה of appearing.

phrases.english: But according to the one who said
all of them are make-up days for the first day,
what does "all" come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's answer that הכל includes one who was lame on the first day and healed on the second
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the view that the later days only make up for the first day, someone exempt on the first day stays exempt, so the lame person cannot be what הכל includes.

steps.title: הכל includes someone blind in one eye
steps.stepSummary: For the view that the days only make up for the first day, הכל comes to include a person who is blind in one eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include someone who is blind in one of his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It gives a new case for הכל: someone who can see with only one eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new case does not depend on the debate about make-up days, because this person's condition is the same on every day of the רגל. So it works for both views about the make-up days. The word הכל teaches that he is obligated to appear even though he is blind in one eye.

keyTerms.meaning: A blind person
In one of his eyes

phrases.english: To include one who is blind in one of his eyes.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers a different case that works for every view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought הכל has nothing to include for the view that the days only make up for the first day.
steps.terutzMaskana: הכל includes a person blind in one eye, who is obligated to appear.

steps.title: A ברייתא exempts someone blind in one eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this answer disagrees with יוחנן בן דהבאי, who says in the name of רבי יהודה that someone blind in one eye is exempt. He learns it from the פסוק, which can be read both as 'will be seen' and 'will see'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not like the following תנא. A ברייתא teaches: יוחנן בן דהבאי says in the name of רבי יהודה that someone blind in one eye is exempt from appearing. The פסוק can be read as 'he will see' and as 'he will be seen'. In the same way that he comes to see, so he comes to be seen. Just as seeing is done with both eyes, so too being seen must be with both eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side note: the answer it just gave goes against a certain תנא. It quotes that תנא's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same Hebrew letters can be read יֵרָאֶה (will be seen) or יִרְאֶה (will see). רבי יהודה links the two readings: a person comes to the מקדש both to see and to be seen. Since full seeing uses two eyes, only someone with two working eyes is obligated, so our answer in Step 9 does not follow his view.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is not according to this תנא
Exempt from the מצוה of appearing in the מקדש
'He will see' / 'he will be seen'. The same letters read two ways

phrases.english: And this is not in line with this תנא,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹחָנָן בֶּן דַּהֲבַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Yochanan ben Dahavai says in the name of Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: סוֹמֵא בְּאַחַת מֵעֵינָיו פָּטוּר מִן הָרְאִיָּיה,
phrases.english: one who is blind in one of his eyes is exempt from appearing,
as it says: "will see," "will be seen"
phrases.notes: שמות 23:17. It's one written word: read with different vowels, it means either 'will see' or 'will be seen.'

phrases.english: in the same way that he comes to see,
so he comes to be seen.
Just as seeing is with both his eyes,
so too being seen is with both his eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that the answer in Step 9 disagrees with a known תנא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to יוחנן בן דהבאי in the name of רבי יהודה, someone blind in one eye is exempt from ראייה, learned from the double reading יִרְאֶה / יֵרָאֶה.

steps.title: Back to the half-slave: two versions of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: A second approach: הכל really does include the half-slave, as first said. רבינא's statement that he is exempt is not a problem, because the two statements follow two different versions of a משנה, an earlier one and a later one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: really it is as we said at first. And what bothered you from רבינא is not a problem. One statement follows the earlier version of the משנה, and the other follows the later version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to answer. It goes back to the first answer, the half-slave, and solves the conflict with רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבינא's view that a half-slave is exempt pushed us to find another case for הכל. Now the גמרא says both opinions are correct, each according to a different stage of a משנה that changed over time. So there is no real contradiction, and the half-slave answer can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another approach)
Really, actually (keeps the earlier answer)
At first, originally
The earlier version of a משנה
The later version of a משנה, after the ruling changed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a seeming argument can come from two different stages of the same משנה, not from a real disagreement.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
really, it is as we said at first,
phrases.notes: This goes back to Step 5: הכל includes someone who is half slave and half free.

phrases.english: and as for what troubled you, that statement of רבינא,
it is not a difficulty:
here, it follows the earlier version of the משנה,
there, it follows the later version of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to Steps 6 through 10 by returning to the answer of Step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two opinions between two versions of a משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבינא's exemption of a half-slave meant הכל could not include him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both can be true. Each follows a different stage of the משנה, so the half-slave answer stands.

steps.title: The משנה about the half-slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source showing an earlier and a later version. According to בית הלל, a half-slave works one day for his master and one day for himself. Then בית שמאי begin their reply, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: someone who is half slave and half free works one day for his master and one day for himself. These are the words of בית הלל. בית שמאי said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that shows the earlier and later versions. It ends by starting בית שמאי's answer, so it is setting up the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's ruling is that the half-slave stays as he is and splits his days between master and himself. The words 'בית שמאי said to them' open their challenge, which will lead to the later version of the משנה. Seeing both versions explains how both statements about the half-slave can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: Works for his master
For himself

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
phrases.english: one who is half slave and half free
works for his master one day
and for himself one day,
these are the words of בית הלל.
בית שמאי said to them:
phrases.notes: Their answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the earlier and later versions mentioned in Step 11
steps.raayaObject: That there was an earlier and a later version of the משנה about a half-slave
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about one who is half slave and half free (also found in פסחים 88a), with בית הלל's view and בית שמאי's reply
